To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the analysis of the cytoplasmic proteome of synoivial tissue is a valuable approach to identify disease specific proteins in chronic inflammatory arthritides.

we investigated the cytosol of synovial biopsy samples from patients with spondyloarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoartrhitis by two‐dimensional protein gel electrophoreses and hierarchical cluster analysis.

the cytosolic protein expression profile of synovial biopsy samples from RA and SpA can be distinguished from OA, and that the expression of calgranulin A MRP‐8 and alpha‐enose are up‐regulated in synovial tissue of SpA and RA patients, but not in OA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins that may contribute to the pathogenesis of chronic inflammatory arthritis.
the identification of disease‐specific proteins that may be useful as biomarkers for diagnosis and monitoring of the disease activity in patients with RA and SpA.
the identification of differentially expressed proteins between RA, SpA, and OA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of MRP‐8 and MRP‐14 is higher in the synovial tissue of SpA patients than in OA patients.
MRP‐8 is the most prominent marker of chronic inflammatory arthritis, and that alpha‐enolases and fructose bisphosphate‐aldolases are more expressed in SpA than OA.
our results support a role of MRP‐8 in the pathophysiology of chronic inflammatory arthritis, and suggest the presence of different pathophysiological pathways in RA and SpAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the analysis of the cytoplasmic proteome of synoviocytes from patients with RA, SpA, and OA is feasible.
we have shown that the proteome analysis is a feasible approach to identify differentially expressed proteins in synovial tissue from patients with chronic inflammatory joint disease.

the analysis of the synovial cytosolic proteomics of chronic inflammatory arthritis, such as SpA and RA, revealed a unique pattern of protein expression that was different from the expression pattern in OA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytosolic protein profile of synovial tissues is different in SpA and RA, and that this approach may provide a useful tool for the diagnosis of SpA.
proteome analysis of inflamed synoviocytes can identify disease‐associated protein expression profiles.
